facts.text: In an open-loop test, the system's output does not change what happens next; in a closed-loop test, the system's actions feed back and alter the situation the system subsequently sees.
facts.quote: In an open-loop test the system's output does not change what happens next, while in a closed-loop test the system's actions feed back and alter the situation it then sees.

facts.text: Open-loop testing is cheap and uses real data, but closed-loop testing is the only way to see the consequences of system actions.
facts.quote: Open loop is cheap and uses real data; closed loop is the only way to see consequences.

facts.text: Before a new system commands braking during recorded-data replay, the recorded machine pose, object poses and sensor measurements are valid historical evidence.
facts.quote: Before the new system commands braking, the recorded machine pose, object poses and sensor measurements are valid historical evidence.

facts.text: The first-divergence point is the first brake command that did not occur in the original recorded run, when the counterfactual machine begins to differ from the recorded machine.
facts.quote: At the first brake command that did not occur in the original run, the counterfactual machine begins to differ from the recorded one.

facts.text: After the first-divergence point, feeding the original sensor record while pretending that the machine has slowed is physically inconsistent.
facts.quote: After that instant, feeding the original sensor record while pretending the machine has slowed is physically inconsistent [Chapter 7].

facts.text: Recorded data can establish whether a new system would have detected an object and requested intervention before a specified time, but cannot establish whether the machine would actually have stopped safely, what subsequent measurements would have been, or whether a worker would have reacted.
facts.quote: Recorded data can therefore answer "would the new system have detected the object and requested intervention before time t?"; they cannot answer "would the machine actually have stopped safely, what would the next measurements have been, or would the worker have reacted?"

facts.text: On-road research in 2024 showed that open-loop planning scores could be matched using the vehicle's own state alone, giving a misleading impression.
facts.quote: On-road research (2024) showed that open-loop planning scores could be matched using the vehicle's own state alone, giving "a misleading impression" [Chapter 7].

facts.text: Teams separate validation metrics by evaluating perception and trigger timing open loop on logs, braking consequences in closed-loop simulation, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) and vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL), and selected stopping outcomes on a proving ground.
facts.quote: Teams therefore split the metrics: perception and trigger timing open loop on logs; braking consequences in closed-loop simulation, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) and vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL); selected stopping outcomes on a proving ground.

facts.text: A log-to-simulation switch branches from the recorded prefix into simulation at the intervention point, with a machine model consuming the brake command and a sensor model regenerating observations.
facts.quote: A "log-to-simulation switch" branches from the recorded prefix into simulation at the intervention point, with a machine model consuming the brake command and a sensor model regenerating the observations [Chapter 7].

facts.text: After a log-to-simulation branch, evidence quality depends on the machine, terrain, actor and sensor models; this limitation is more serious off-road because soil, grade, payload and dust are more variable than paved-road dynamics.
facts.quote: After the branch, the evidence is only as good as the machine, terrain, actor and sensor models, a warning the booklet calls more serious off-road, where soil, grade, payload and dust are more variable than paved-road dynamics [Chapter 7].

facts.text: Shadow mode and replay are open loop; software-in-the-loop (SIL), hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) and vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL) are normally closed loop; semantic replay can be either open or closed loop.
facts.quote: Shadow mode and replay are open loop; software-in-the-loop (SIL), HIL and VIL are normally closed loop; semantic replay can be either [Chapters 1, 7].

facts.text: The existing warning fleet can supply enormous open-loop evidence immediately, but because the new function changes machine motion, validation must keep three evidence classes separate: the measured recorded prefix, model-dependent post-intervention simulation, and selected measured real stops covering few cases.
facts.quote: three evidence classes must be kept apart: the recorded prefix (measured), post-intervention simulation (model-dependent), and selected real stops (measured, few cases) [Chapter 7].
